Before anybody else joins — the south region line. Eighteen per cent above budget. Do you know why yet?
Not with certainty, but I have three candidates. It must be the new contract that started in May. The timing lines up and the amount is almost the same.
Almost the same, or the same?
Almost. It accounts for about eighty per cent of the increase. The rest could be a spike in freight, because the fuel index moved in the same month.
And is any of it just the time of year?
It might be partly seasonality, since we see something similar every June, although this year is bigger. I would have to check that one before I commit to it.
Fine. Is there any chance somebody booked it twice?

It cannot be that. We checked every entry above ten thousand and they all traced back correctly, so we are not overstating anything. And you — do you want the three reasons in the note, or only the first one?
What I am sure about is the total. To be certain about the split, I would need one more day.

One thing I have learned from sitting on the other side of these calls. When somebody says a number is definitely something, and then twenty minutes later it turns out to be something else, I do not remember the number. I remember the word definitely. And after that, every figure that person gives me carries a small tax. Now, here is the part that surprises people. Saying I am not certain does not cost you anything at all, as long as you say what you are certain about first, and as long as you say how sure you are. It must be the new supplier, because nothing else changed. It might be a timing difference, but I would have to check. That cannot be currency, because the rate barely moved. Three different levels, three different words, and every one of them is more useful to me than a confident guess.

The variance came in at eighteen per cent and the first thing everybody wanted was a reason. So let me give you the three we looked at, in order of how likely they are. It must be the new contract in the south region. It started in May, the timing lines up exactly, and the amount is almost the same. That is the one I would put my money on. It could also be a spike in freight, because the fuel index moved in the same month, but freight is a small part of this line, so it cannot explain the whole difference on its own. And it may be partly seasonality, since we see something similar every June, although this year is bigger than usual. What it cannot be is a posting error, because we checked every entry above ten thousand and they all traced back correctly.
